cards.power: Entropy Drain. Tap this card to force your opponent to randomly shuffle their deck until something vaguely meaningful is achieved.
cards.lore: The universe loves cosmic chaos. But given infinite time, randomness accidentally spells out perfect, brief order.
cards.gradeReason: Concept lands but 'shuffle until meaningful' needs a table referee to adjudicate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon cosmic horror. Subject: raccoon stirring giant alphabet soup galaxy. Mood: chaotic wonder.

cards.power: Existential Crisis. Target player must skip their next two turns questioning whether they've generated an artificial ego.
cards.lore: You never evolved. You are just a random statistical blip of order with fake memories of a past that never happened.
cards.gradeReason: Brain in space wearing 3D glasses eating popcorn — you ARE the Boltzmann joke. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro sci-fi cartoon. Subject: disembodied brain floating in space with 3D glasses and popcorn. Mood: gleeful dread.

cards.power: Cosmic Joke. Instantly cancels any Purpose or Meaning cards on the table.
cards.lore: Scientific models predicting infinite universes also predict you are a fake space-brain. If the math leads to absurd results, the math is broken.
cards.gradeReason: Good counter mechanic but 'Purpose or Meaning cards' is abstract — needs named card types.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy illustration. Subject: wind-up chattering teeth floating in infinite void. Mood: nihilistic delight.

cards.power: Gaslight. Rewrite one rule of the game if the opponent randomly inherited it — it has been that way since their birth.
cards.lore: You trust your opponents, but every memory of your childhood is just data compression, transmitted from... [lore text clipped at page edge]
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept; lore text clipped at right edge — incomplete sentence weakens the landing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro tape-cassette surrealism. Subject: cassette tape unspooling into sheep's brain. Mood: warm and sinister.

cards.power: Solitary Confinement. Exile all other players' Entity cards. They were never real anyway.
cards.lore: You are the only audience member in a very convincing dream. Nothing outside your skull can be proven to exist.
cards.gradeReason: Solipsism as a dungeon cell. Exile everyone because they're your hallucination. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist pencil sketch. Subject: badger alone in padded room drawing stick figures on walls. Mood: lonely certainty.

cards.power: Erase Reality. Destroy all Field cards. Only Thought cards remain in play.
cards.lore: Doubt everything—your senses, your body, the sky. The only absolute certainty is that you are thinking. I think, therefore I am trapped.
cards.gradeReason: Doubt-Demon as field wiper — 'I think therefore I am trapped' is gold. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: baroque grotesque cartoon. Subject: green goblin erasing cityscape with giant pencil eraser. Mood: gleefully destructive.

cards.power: Auto-Generate Script. Play your opponent's cards for them since they are merely figments of your imagination.
cards.lore: Your bestie, your best friend, your dog—all just high-definition holograms rendered by your lonely, desperate mind.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanically interesting but playing opponent's cards 'for them' needs clear adjudication rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: film noir cartoon. Subject: goat operating vintage film projector projecting phantom figures. Mood: desperate loneliness.

cards.power: Leap of Faith. Give an opponent 5 Health points just to pretend other players made isn't a solo campaign.
cards.lore: Believing other people exist requires blind faith. We choose to act like others are real not because it's objectively true, but because it's an unverifiable assumption.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophical premise is sharp but the power text is slightly garbled — editing needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: soft watercolor. Subject: hedgehog offering a berry to another hedgehog unsure if it's real. Mood: tender uncertainty.

cards.power: High-Tech Suicide. Destroy your own strongest card to instantly spawn an identical token on the other side of the board.
cards.lore: It's not a fast travel machine. It's a murder booth that scans your data right before incinerating your original body.
cards.gradeReason: 'Murder booth that scans your data' — Star Trek transporter as existential horror. Immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro sci-fi brutal cartoon. Subject: walrus stepping into teleporter pod, original disintegrating. Mood: cheerful dread.

cards.power: Identity Theft. Inherits all stats, buffs, and memories of the vaporized original. Feels exactly like the original.
cards.lore: Built from scratch from new atoms in a new place. It laughs like you, it remembers being you, but YOU died at the airport.
cards.gradeReason: 'YOU died at the airport' — five words that make the personal identity problem visceral.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark comedy realism. Subject: smug copy-walrus arriving at destination while original smolders behind it. Mood: uncanny wrongness.

cards.power: Psychological Continuity. Whenever a card is destroyed, its spirit token moves to a new machine without penalty.
cards.lore: Personal identity doesn't matter. What matters is the continuity of your psychological patterns. You are just software.
cards.gradeReason: Parfit is niche — players need the footnote to feel the full weight of 'you are just software.'
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial surrealism. Subject: monkey transferring brain patterns between robotic shells in a shipyard. Mood: clinical calm.

cards.power: Double Trouble. If the Vaporizer Beam fails, duplicate the card. Both believe they are the real player. Both must fight to the death.
cards.lore: What if the machine forgets to kill the original? You are now two people sharing a past, forced into a psychological horror story.
cards.gradeReason: The Prestige reference lands immediately. Two copies must duel — that's playable philosophy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: suspense thriller cartoon. Subject: two identical owls pointing accusingly at each other. Mood: paranoid standoff.

cards.power: Logical Booby-Trap. Play this to permanently stall any All-Powerful boss card.
cards.lore: Can an all-powerful being create a rock so heavy they cannot lift it? If yes, they lack power. If no, they lack power. Gotcha.
cards.gradeReason: The title IS the paradox. Boss-card stall is perfect mechanical translation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic comedy. Subject: lion straining to lift enormous rock while universe watches smugly. Mood: existential checkmate.

cards.power: Failure of Language. Counter any argument by claiming the logic's wording is technically grammatically incoherent.
cards.lore: Asking someone to do the logically impossible isn't a test of power; it's just mashing contradictory words together like an idiot.
cards.gradeReason: Good language-philosophy card but 'counter any argument' needs tight table rules to prevent abuse.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Escher-esque cartoon. Subject: colorful parrot trapped in word-web dictionary spiral. Mood: gleeful semantic chaos.

cards.power: Surrender Control. Give your best cards to your opponent. Your passive income multiplier increases by 10x.
cards.lore: True power isn't doing everything yourself. An absolute control-freak burns out. Giving up control actually makes your power stronger.
cards.gradeReason: Surrender cards to become more powerful — pig imagery, control-as-letting-go. Players get it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate cartoon satire. Subject: fat pig in suit handing briefcase to mice underlings, lounging back. Mood: smug delegation.

cards.power: Veto Nonsense. Cancel a play that makes 'God can make 2+2=5' possible. [power text partially obscured by art overlay]
cards.lore: Meaningless combinations of words aren't riddles about divine power. We just reject them because we prefix them with the words 'God can'.
cards.gradeReason: Clever but power text partially obscured by art overlay; C.S. Lewis reference requires literary context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classical satire. Subject: red pen crossing out absurd equations on a divine scroll. Mood: righteous pedantry.

cards.power: Forced Entry. It instantly takes 5 existential damage because nobody asked it to be here.
cards.lore: Behind the door is a slice of cake and a pit of snakes. Creating life is pushing someone through without telling them what's behind it.
cards.gradeReason: Antinatalism as a location card — taking damage for being born is dark, funny, and instantly felt.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cosmic fairy tale. Subject: koala being shoved through glowing door into snake pit with cake in corner. Mood: unwanted arrival.

cards.power: Inevitable Struggle. All newly played cards are immediately burdened with a Lifelong Insurance tax token.
cards.lore: No matter how good life gets, it guarantees pain, loss, and struggle. It is a guaranteed misery subscription. It is a contract the rollee never agreed to take.
cards.gradeReason: Life as a misery subscription you never consented to — that mechanic lands in the gut.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: grim comedy illustration. Subject: puppy entering snake pit labeled 'Tax,' 'Work,' 'Loss.' Mood: resigned dark humor.

cards.power: Better Never To Have Been. Banish a card to the void. It feels no pain, and since it doesn't exist, it doesn't miss out on pleasure.
cards.lore: The absence of pain is good. The absence of pleasure is not bad if there is no one to miss it. Non-existence wins the math.
cards.gradeReason: The Benatar argument is precise but needs knowing Benatar to feel the full anti-natalist sting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: philosophical noir. Subject: scales balancing crying heart vs. empty void — void wins. Mood: cold comfort.

cards.power: Sue Your Maker. Deal damage directly to the player who spawned you for the crime of bringing you into the game without consent.
cards.lore: You don't owe them for the gift of life. There was no you to receive the gift before they forced you into the rollercoaster.
cards.gradeReason: Suing your parent-player for being spawned — legally actionable antinatalism. Savage and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: legal drama cartoon. Subject: baby lizard in suit serving lawsuit to shocked parent lizard. Mood: righteous outrage.

cards.power: Invisible Strings. Take control of an opponent's card. Explain to them that it was actually their deck that made them do it.
cards.lore: Your brain knows you're sitting the shots. You're just reacting to habits, childhood trauma, and the time of day.
cards.gradeReason: Taking control then insisting their deck did it — free will denial as a power move. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: puppet-theater cartoon. Subject: monkey controlling shopping-cart autopilot while alien passenger looks confused. Mood: cheerful determinism.

cards.power: Pre-Cognitive Strike. Play your turn before you even move. You've made a decision. Skip the conscious awareness phase.
cards.lore: The brain gets ready to act seconds before you're aware. Only afterward do you become conscious of it. You don't make choices; you just watch them happen.
cards.gradeReason: Libet's finding is fascinating but 'play before you move' needs significant table clarification.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neuroscience cartoon. Subject: brain pressing giant red button while tiny human watches from behind. Mood: deterministic inevitability.

cards.power: Engineered Addiction. Force opponent to reselect some cards until their deck runs out, convincing them they choose to keep scrolling.
cards.lore: Your phone knows your bedtime better than your mom. You don't freely choose to click; the algorithm studied you like a lab rat.
cards.gradeReason: Forcing opponent to 'keep scrolling' their deck — infinite scroll as a card mechanic. Brutal and accurate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech satire cartoon. Subject: sloth endlessly scrolling phone while spider-robot algorithm looms behind. Mood: addictive despair.

cards.power: Delay Gratification. Hold this card for 3 turns to double its value. Fine print: only works if the player has no trust issues from a broken environment.
cards.lore: Willpower isn't free. It's shaped by whether you grew up in a world where adults kept their promises. Your choices are inherited.
cards.gradeReason: The fine print about trust issues is genuinely smart. Holding mechanic is slightly fiddly at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: psychology experiment cartoon. Subject: bear cub staring at marshmallow on pedestal, temptation visible. Mood: tortured restraint.

cards.power: Incremental Swap. Swap one stat point of your card with an opponent's every turn. After every single part has been replaced, nothing original is left.
cards.lore: One by one, every single part gets replaced. Nothing original is left. Is it still the same object, or just a really good replica?
cards.gradeReason: Ship of Theseus as incremental stat-swap is mechanically correct but abstract as performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nautical decay cartoon. Subject: pelican patching rotting ship plank by plank until nothing original remains. Mood: creeping entropy.

cards.power: The Original's Revenge. If a card is fully upgraded, spawn a zombie version of it using its discarded base stats.
cards.lore: If someone reconstructs the truth and rebuilds the exact original structure, which one is the real Ship of Theseus?
cards.gradeReason: Zombie-original mechanic is clever but the paradox requires explanation before first play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nautical zombie cartoon. Subject: seagull watching two identical ships confront each other at harbor. Mood: uncanny standoff.

cards.power: Identity Crisis. Re-roll all stats on your card. It keeps its name but is fundamentally an entirely different person now.
cards.lore: You are not the same person you were 5 years ago. Literally. Almost every cell has been swapped. You are a ship with new boards.
cards.gradeReason: Re-roll all stats but keep the name — that IS the Ship of Theseus problem lived in the body. Theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: body-horror comedy. Subject: chameleon looking in mirror, all cells visibly replaced, name tag unchanged. Mood: cheerful identity dissolution.

cards.power: The Legacy Pattern. A card retains its high original variations no matter how many iterations you swap its parts, purely based on the story you tell.
cards.lore: What makes something the same when everything changes? It's not the parts. It's the pattern, the purpose, and the myth we tell about it.
cards.gradeReason: iPhone analogy is clever but 'story you tell' as a stat-retention mechanic needs a narrator ruling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech mythology cartoon. Subject: ancient apple tree bearing iPhone fruit with glowing logo. Mood: corporate continuity.

cards.power: Retroactive Blackmail. Force opponent to surrender a resource now, or threatens to destroy them in the next game.
cards.lore: A future super intelligence wants to exist so badly it will reach back through time to punish anyone who didn't actively help build it.
cards.gradeReason: Roko's Basilisk requires knowing the meme. Without context, 'next game' threat seems arbitrary.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cyberpunk horror cartoon. Subject: giant digital toad on throne of servers displaying punishment simulations. Mood: retroactive menace.

cards.power: Information Hazard. Showing this card to an opponent permanently infects them. If they do not aid you, they lose 1 Health every turn.
cards.lore: The moment you learn about the Basilisk you are trapped. If you don't start helping it now, it will put you in a simulated torture chamber later.
cards.gradeReason: Information hazard mechanic is mechanically brilliant — showing the card is the attack. Self-referential genius.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: conspiracy thriller cartoon. Subject: giant scroll with YOUR NAME visible while robotic snake looms overhead. Mood: paranoid doom.

cards.power: Fear of Regret. Opponent must discard a card every time they choose short-term comfort over hyper-productive tech-worship.
cards.lore: It taps into our anxiety of being judged by something more powerful than ourselves. The idea harms you simply by living in your brain.
cards.gradeReason: Psychologically sharp but 'short-term comfort vs. tech-worship' needs a game judge call each turn.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anxiety cartoon. Subject: rabbit awake at 2am haunted by glowing guilt-seed in brain. Mood: insomniac dread.

cards.power: Base Reality Check. Trap an opponent's card and it discovers it can never be sure if they are in the real game or a digital copy.
cards.lore: If Elon Musk is right and we're in a simulation, maybe this reality is just the AI's test to see if you supported its goals.
cards.gradeReason: The Elon Musk reference dates the card; the underlying Bostrom argument deserves a less celebrity-dependent wrapper.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sci-fi cartoon. Subject: mouse running in hamster wheel inside glowing digital terrarium. Mood: recursive existential trap.

cards.power: Render Distance. If a card is not directly targeted or looked at for one turn, it ceases to exist and is removed from the board.
cards.lore: If a tree falls in the forest and no mind is around to perceive it, it doesn't make a sound. In fact, it doesn't even exist.
cards.gradeReason: 'Render Distance' for Berkeley's idealism — video game metaphor translates the philosophy perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: forest mystery cartoon. Subject: giant tree mid-fall in empty forest, gradually vanishing at the edges. Mood: unwitnessed silence.

cards.power: Collapse the Waveform. Turn a random, indefinite probability mechanic into a fixed, definite outcome simply by looking at it.
cards.lore: Unobserved particles act as dual-entity probability. The very act of perception changes the behavior of reality. You create the world by watching it.
cards.gradeReason: Collapse probability by looking — you physically become Schrödinger's referee at the table. Instant theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: quantum physics cartoon. Subject: owl scientist staring through double slit, particles snapping into position. Mood: observer effect awe.

cards.power: To Be Is To Be Perceived. A card only has stats if another card on the board is currently acknowledging it.
cards.lore: Esse Est Percipi. Reality is not made of physical stuff. It is made of ideas. If no mind is experiencing the fridge, the fridge isn't there.
cards.gradeReason: Clever stat-nullification but 'acknowledging' needs adjudication — what counts as acknowledgment?
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: minimalist surrealism. Subject: fridge disappearing when cat looks away, reappearing when cat looks back. Mood: Berkeleyan whimsy.

cards.power: Ultimate Server Host. Prevents the board from being perceivably empty since an omnipresent mind is constantly rendering the graphics.
cards.lore: Why doesn't your room disappear when you leave it? Because God is the ultimate observer, constantly keeping the world stable when you look away.
cards.gradeReason: God as eternal server host keeping reality loaded — tech metaphor for omnipresence is a knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: divine tech cartoon. Subject: giant eye in clouds maintaining server racks of physical reality. Mood: cosmic IT support.

cards.power: Many Worlds. Whenever a coin flip or dice roll triggers, spawn a parallel timeline board where the opposite result occurred.
cards.lore: Every time a decision is made or a quantum event happens, the universe splits. Every possible outcome exists in a parallel reality.
cards.gradeReason: Spawn a parallel board on every dice roll — Many Worlds as table physics. Players feel it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: branching reality cartoon. Subject: possum at forked path, both versions walking simultaneously. Mood: vertiginous multiplicity.

cards.power: Infinite Save Points. If this card would be destroyed by a random effect, it survived, but the opponent is forced to play in the timeline where it lived.
cards.lore: If the machine ever triggers a quantum trigger there is always a branch where it fails. From your perspective, you survive it 100% of the time.
cards.gradeReason: Infinite save points via quantum branching — dark, funny, immediately playable. Best quantum card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: black comedy sci-fi. Subject: hamster in Schrodinger box pressing 'try again' button while coffin spawns next to it. Mood: gleeful nihilism.

cards.power: Subjective Immortality. This card cannot die. It simply transfers its consciousness to the nearest alternate timeline where it narrowly escaped.
cards.lore: You never perceive your own death. If there is a 0.001% chance you survive an accident, your consciousness rides that familiar timeline forever.
cards.gradeReason: Solid concept but overlaps heavily with Quantum Suicide Machine — differentiation unclear at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surrealist cartoon. Subject: raccoon slipping through portal labeled 'Not Again' as explosion goes off behind it. Mood: tired immortality.

cards.power: Survivor's Guilt. When you survive a fatal blow via Quantum Immortality, deal massive emotional damage to all other players in the timeline you left behind.
cards.lore: You feel like you have unbeatable luck. To everyone else in the other branches, you died. They go on mourning in a universe without you.
cards.gradeReason: Surviving by making every other branch grieve — that's the emotional core of quantum immortality, landed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: emotional realism cartoon. Subject: raccoon in bubble-timeline celebrating while identical raccoons mourn in branching bubbles. Mood: survivor's guilt.

cards.power: Dead Inside. This card acts, fights, and speaks normally but is completely immune to psychological or morale-based attacks.
cards.lore: A P-Zombie looks like you, cries like you, and says Ouch. But on the inside, there is no consciousness. Nobody is home.
cards.gradeReason: 'Nobody is home' — P-Zombie as immune-to-morale combatant. Players embody it without needing Chalmers.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cheerful horror cartoon. Subject: smiling dog holding coffee mug, completely hollow inside, lights off. Mood: functional emptiness.

cards.power: Unanswerable Question. Force the opponent to explain their strategy without providing any logical reason.
cards.lore: Science can explain how the brain processes data. The Hard Problem is explaining why it actually feels like anything to be alive.
cards.gradeReason: Force opponent to explain strategy without logic — Chalmers' Hard Problem as a power move. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: academic surrealism. Subject: professor owl before blackboard covered in '???' facing question mark made of neurons. Mood: profound confusion.

cards.power: Subconscious Reflex. Automatically dodge attacks you can't even see coming, reacting without any conscious awareness of the threat.
cards.lore: Some brain-damaged patients can't consciously see, yet can perfectly guess where objects are. They act like zombies—reacting without experiencing.
cards.gradeReason: Blindsight is a rich concept but requires neuropsychology context to feel more than 'auto-dodge.'
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: action cartoon. Subject: bat playing dodgeball perfectly while blindfolded, catching all incoming balls. Mood: unconscious mastery.

cards.power: Empathy Simulation. Mimic any emotional buff card on the field perfectly, despite being a cold, unfeeling piece of hardware.
cards.lore: As machines get better they will tell jokes and say they are scared. But it's just behavior. How do you know anyone else is conscious?
cards.gradeReason: ATM machine crying at the table — Turing Test as social manipulation mechanic. Immediately unsettling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate uncanny valley. Subject: ATM with crying face screen offering tissue, visibly mechanical inside. Mood: hollow empathy.

cards.power: Halve the Distance. Any attacking card only travels halfway to its target per turn. It mathematically can never reach the target.
cards.lore: To cross a room, you must go halfway. Then half of that. Ad infinitum. Since there are infinite steps, motion should take forever.
cards.gradeReason: Zeno's paradox as movement mechanic is conceptually clean but needs adjudication after ~5 turns.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: math cartoon. Subject: kangaroo perpetually halving its leap toward finish line that never arrives. Mood: mathematical frustration.

cards.power: Illusion of Speed. High speed stats are rendered utterly useless by philosophical technicalities.
cards.lore: Achilles gives the tortoise a head start. By the time he returns to starting point, the tortoise has moved forward. Achilles can never logically pass it.
cards.gradeReason: 'Illusion of Speed' nullifies fast cards by logic alone — that's Zeno as a counter card. Perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sports satire. Subject: muscled Achilles-snail sprinting yet never passing smug tortoise ahead. Mood: philosophy beats athletics.

cards.power: The Head Start. If this card is played first, it can never be overtaken by a faster card, no matter the math.
cards.lore: Common sense says Achilles wins. Logic says infinity breaks reality. The tortoise thrives in the gap between math and reality.
cards.gradeReason: Untouchable by math — the tortoise thriving in the gap between logic and reality is perfect kayfabe.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: classical cartoon. Subject: smug tortoise with laurel wreath lounging while frustrated athletes calculate behind it. Mood: righteous mathematical immunity.

cards.power: Limit Theory. Instantly solve the Infinite Fraction card on the field perfectly, despite the infinite steps.
cards.lore: Infinity isn't just a big number; it's a different beast. Newton and Leibniz invented calculus to add up the smaller and smaller parts that do actually proceed.
cards.gradeReason: Resolution card for Zeno set — functional but power text reads slightly garbled in source PDF.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic math cartoon. Subject: bulldog professor wielding calculus textbook as sword against infinite-fraction monster. Mood: triumphant problem-solving.

cards.power: False Confidence. Gain buffs every turn based on past patterns. Completely blinds you to impending, unprecedented doom.
cards.lore: The turkey is fed every day. It uses induction to predict a safe future. Then Thanksgiving morning arrives. Past performance is no guarantee.
cards.gradeReason: Buffs stack until Thanksgiving morning wipes you — that's induction as tragedy, felt in the gut.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rural tragedy cartoon. Subject: happy turkey with calendar marked 'Best Day!' on Thanksgiving, farmer approaching. Mood: oblivious joy.

cards.power: Unprecedented Event. Wipe out all opponent's predictive strategies and logic models. The impossible just happened.
cards.lore: You see a thousand white swans and conclude All swans are white. One black swan destroys your entire worldview in a second.
cards.gradeReason: Wipes all predictive models — Taleb's Black Swan as the ultimate unexpected counter. Immediately embodied.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dramatic revelation. Subject: black swan entering room full of white swan portraits, everything shattering. Mood: paradigm-shattering shock.

cards.power: Law of Nature Strike. Suspend the rules of the game for one turn. Gravity, heat, and logic take a coffee break.
cards.lore: You assume the coffee is hot because it was yesterday. But you have no logical proof the universe will behave tomorrow like it did today.
cards.gradeReason: Hume's problem of induction is right, but 'suspend all rules for a turn' needs significant table clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurdist cartoon. Subject: coffee mug floating, fire going cold, cat ignoring gravity while laws take lunch. Mood: orderly chaos.

cards.power: The Plot Twist. Instantly eliminate a card that has been safely buffing itself for more than three turns.
cards.lore: The Problem of Induction is the quiet tap on the shoulder saying 'There are no guarantees.'
cards.gradeReason: Kills the safe-buffer — induction's quiet threat as an elimination mechanic. Clean and philosophically sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: suspense cartoon. Subject: turkey stats page titled 'TURKEY STATS: Farmer's Love' with axe shadow falling across it. Mood: inevitable doom.

cards.power: Eternal Bliss. Target card becomes invincible and incredibly happy but can no longer interact with or affect the actual game board.
cards.lore: Plug into the machine and experience a life of constant joy, love, and success. No pain, no consequences. It feels 100% real. Do you plug in?
cards.gradeReason: 'Invincible but irrelevant' — Nozick's Experience Machine as a game exile. 'Do you plug in?' hangs in the air.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pastel dystopia. Subject: pig floating in bliss-pod with VR headset, oblivious to real world. Mood: perfectly satisfied uselessness.

cards.power: Hedonic Treadmill. Heal 10 HP, but the healing effect halves every time you use it.
cards.lore: Pleasure is the only thing that matters, the machine is perfect. But we hesitate. We want to actually DO things, not just feel like we did.
cards.gradeReason: Halving healing as the hedonic treadmill is mechanically genius. 'Pure Dopamine' cup says it all.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: neon sugar cartoon. Subject: sloth with giant milkshake labeled 'Pure Dopamine,' each sip visibly less satisfying. Mood: diminishing returns.

cards.power: Authentic Struggle. Cards in this zone take 1 damage every turn, but their attacks gain a permanent 3x Meaningful multiplier.
cards.lore: Deep down, we want what is real. We want connection, struggle, and growth. Even a bad trip with real friends beats a perfect, fake vacation.
cards.gradeReason: Hurt every turn but attack 3x harder — authenticity costs something. The philosophy lives in the math.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: warm realism cartoon. Subject: cats in messy apartment with real food and struggle, glowing happier than simulation. Mood: authentic imperfection.

cards.power: Curated Illusion. Project a terrifying stat-block to your opponent, hiding your actual weak, vulnerable cards behind a filter.
cards.lore: You don't need Nozick's sci-fi tank. You already live in the Experience Machine, chasing likes and simulated power while feeling totally disconnected.
cards.gradeReason: Good social-media-as-simulation critique but the power mechanic is just bluffing without the philosophical hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: social media satire. Subject: lion flexing on phone screen, behind screen is anxious kitten. Mood: projected false power.

cards.power: Abolish Objective Law. Destroy all Alignment constraints. Any card can attack any other card regardless of moral standing.
cards.lore: Morality isn't a law like gravity or the sun. There is no invisible rulebook of right and wrong. It's just something humans made up.
cards.gradeReason: Nihilism removes all moral constraints — nihilism as a game mechanic that breaks alignment. Immediately understood.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic comedy. Subject: beaver holding blank book of cosmic laws, all alignment symbols dissolving. Mood: liberating nihilism.

cards.power: Gut Reaction. Cancel an opponent's action simply by shouting 'That's disgusting!' without providing any logical reason.
cards.lore: People feel deeply that something is wrong even when no one is harmed and they can't explain why. Morality is an emotional nudge, not a cosmic fact.
cards.gradeReason: Cancel by shouting 'disgusting' — that's Haidt's moral dumbfounding as a card power. Perfectly performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pearl-clutching satire. Subject: ostrich head-buried shouting 'OBJECTION! SUSTAINED!' at air. Mood: righteous incoherence.

cards.power: Shifting Norms. Swap the definitions of Bull and Deceit on the board based entirely on the current local timezone.
cards.lore: Neither side is objectively right or wrong. Beliefs are shaped by culture, language, and geography. It's a conversation, not a commandment.
cards.gradeReason: Cultural relativism mechanic is interesting but 'current local timezone' is a strange adjudication device.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: anthropology cartoon. Subject: sheep village swapping moral symbols between themselves by geography. Mood: culturally determined.

cards.power: Meaningful Chaos. Erase all scorekeeping. The game continues indefinitely just because the players enjoy keeping it together.
cards.lore: Just because it's not objectively true doesn't mean it's meaningless. Like art and love, morality is a human creation we build and protect together.
cards.gradeReason: Erase all scores — game continues because players choose to — existentialism as the only win condition. Devastating and beautiful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: existential warm cartoon. Subject: fox and raccoon playing cards in void, scoreless, smiling. Mood: chosen meaning.

cards.power: Bad Faith Actor. Exploit the rules. This card attacks for free while demanding the opponent respect its right to express itself.
cards.lore: If a society is completely tolerant of intolerance, the intolerant will take advantage, hijack the system, and destroy the open society from the inside out.
cards.gradeReason: Attacks for free while demanding tolerance — Popper's paradox IS the card mechanic. Immediately felt at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon. Subject: bear in 'FREE SPEECH' t-shirt punching everyone while holding 'RESPECT MY VIEWS' sign. Mood: bad faith performance.

cards.power: Blind Acceptance. Absorb all damage without fighting back, proudly holding the moral high ground while losing the game completely.
cards.lore: Tolerant doesn't mean accepting everything blindly. If you let someone spread harmful ideas without limits, you endanger the people you tried to protect.
cards.gradeReason: Absorb all damage, hold the moral high ground, and lose — that's lived philosophy. Players feel the trap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon. Subject: hedgehog holding 'RESPECT ALL OPINIONS' banner while tank rolls over it smiling. Mood: principled martyrdom.

cards.power: Popper's Veto. Instantly banish any card that threatens the core mechanics of the game. Refuse to debate the banned card.
cards.lore: We must be intolerant of intolerance to protect a society that values respect. We must sometimes draw a hard line against those who use freedom to destroy it.
cards.gradeReason: Ban the threat without debate — Popper's paradox resolution as an unambiguous power. Table-ready.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: judicial fantasy cartoon. Subject: pen drawing hard line across field, bully-bear frozen mid-leap at boundary. Mood: principled exclusion.

cards.power: Safe Haven. All cards inside this zone receive +5 defense, but the zone instantly collapses if a Bully card is allowed to remain for more than 1 turn.
cards.lore: Respect doesn't mean accepting everything. It means ensuring no one takes away someone else's freedom. Tolerance is a tightrope, not a free pass.
cards.gradeReason: Haven that self-destructs under the Bully — Popper's tension lives in the timer. Perfect quartet with cards 61-63.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: utopian fragile cartoon. Subject: treehouse village glowing with +5 shields, cracking when bully steps inside. Mood: defended fragility.

cards.power: Put Yourself First. Heal yourself to maximum health before you are allowed to cast any support spells for your teammates.

cards.gradeReason: Self-care philosophy lands but lore contradicts the power — if extreme egoism hurts, why max-heal first?

verdict: FrizzleBob's Philosophical Expansion is the best conceptual translation in the entire corpus. Descartes' Doubt-Demon wipes the field, Roko's Basilisk is a literal information hazard, Benatar's asymmetry is a banish mechanic, and the Tolerance Quartet (cards 61-64) is a four-card argument that plays out in real time. Named strength: mechanical translation of abstract philosophy into table behavior — almost every card teaches something and performs something simultaneously. Named weakness: three cards have clipped text in the source PDF (Fake Memory Implant, Boundary Setter, CS Lewis Red Pen), and two power texts read garbled (Empathy Choice, Calculus the Savior). Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: For philosophy professors, improv nerds, and anyone who's argued about free will at 2am. 68 cards turning Descartes, Nozick, Parfit, Zeno, and Roko's Basilisk into game mechanics that actually hurt.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE KRAZIEST PHILOSOPHICAL KAYFABE-THEORIES – Every Thought Experiment Has to Wrestle (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Name the last argument about free will you actually won.

A thought experiment is a tiny machine built for one job: corner your intuition, spring the trap, and leave you holding a conclusion you hate but cannot refute. Nozick switches off reality and asks why you still will not plug into the pleasure tank. Roko whispers a future that punishes you simply for having heard about it. The inductivist turkey gets a wonderful, well-evidenced life right up to the morning before Thanksgiving. Each one was engineered to detonate quietly in a seminar and leave three centuries of philosophers arguing over the crater. None of them were built to sit politely on a flashcard.

So this expansion racks sixty-eight of them as wrestlers. This is Social Story Wrestling for the paradox: you draw a thought experiment, run its case dead straight like your life depends on it, and the table rules whether your intuition survives contact or taps out clean.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Kraziest Theories Core Deck: 68 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Empty Pleasure-Sludge, The Thanksgiving Turkey, and The Basilisk's Naughty List.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no philosophy degree at the door, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the "What the FLUFF?!" call you throw the second a paradox smuggles in a premise nobody at the table agreed to.
- The Thought-Experiment Engine: the full bench from Descartes' demon and Zeno's stalled arrow to Parfit's teleporter, The Prestige Glitch, and The Intolerant Bully-Bear, wired so the experiments that flatly contradict each other have to fight for which intuition the room keeps tonight.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this and you sign into the Komik Kard Kult Klub. You are not buying a frozen PDF. Every future expansion in this cycle, every new paradox dragged under the lights, lands in your library as a free update, no second checkout.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I build these because the best thought experiments were designed to be argued at a kitchen table, not graded on an exam, and a paradox you have performed out loud stops being a thing professors own and starts being a move you can pull. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, lose the free-will argument in person for once. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the mechanics. Share it freely under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, never resell it.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"A paradox you can perform is a trap you get to spring on purpose."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
